required_fixes: In inequality (1), justify the intermediate step δ(L) ≤ ℓ1: this uses δ(L∖{ℓ1}) ≥ 0, which holds because for a sorted nonnegative list the alternating sum beginning with a plus on the largest element is nonnegative (pair ℓ2≥ℓ3, ℓ4≥ℓ5, ...). One sentence would close this minor gap; alternatively note δ(L) ≤ Σ(odd-position entries) ≤ ΣL directly.
verified_claims: Lemma 1: pairing-strategy proof that the alternating-pick value is exactly odd(S); both the Liu-side pairing (v2,v3),(v4,v5),... and the Xiang-side pairing (v1,v2),(v3,v4),... arguments are correct.
Lemma 2: deleting an equal pair {x,x} from a sorted multiset preserves δ, since the x-block's length parity and starting index are unchanged and later entries shift by two positions.
Lemma E base case r=1: two pieces exceeding 2^{n-1} must both lie inside the unique part of size 2^n, giving v2 ≤ 2^{n-1}.
Lemma E inductive step: if v_{2r} > 2^{n-r}, the 2r largest pieces lie in parts of sizes 2^{n-r+1},...,2^n of total 2^{n+1}-2^{n-r+1}, and 2Σv_{2i} ≤ Σ_{i≤2r}v_i yields the bound.
Lower bound: with M ≤ 2n+1 pieces, r = ⌊M/2⌋ ≤ n, so even(S) ≤ 2^n - 1 in units of 1/N, hence Liu guarantees 2^n/N.
Pigeonhole on the 2^{n+1} subset sums with N = 2^{n+1}-1 gaps in [0,1] gives disjoint nonempty-complement P,Q with |ΣP - ΣQ| ≤ 1/N after cancelling the intersection.
Cancellation procedure: each split is one interior cut adding one piece; counting gives c ≤ |P|+|Q|-1 (whether ℓ ≥ 1 or ℓ = 0 with a final equality step), so total cuts ≤ |Z| + |P|+|Q| - 1 = n.
The leftover from cancellation has total exactly D ≤ 1/N, and δ of the final multiset equals δ(L) ≤ ΣL ≤ 1/N by Lemmas 2 and (1); the case with one of P,Q empty also works with ≤ n cuts.
Degenerate cases: m ≤ n (halve everything, δ = 0); M = 1 or small M in Lemma E; n = 1 gives c = 2/3, checked by hand.
All Xiang cut points are interior to Liu's parts, so they are distinct from Liu's marks and from each other.
summary: The proposed value c_n = 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) is established by a complete and correct two-sided argument. The claiming phase is exactly solved by the standard pairing/mirroring argument (Lemma 1). The lower bound uses an elegant induction (Lemma E) exploiting the dyadic part sizes. The upper bound combines a pigeonhole argument on subset sums, halving of neutral parts, and a greedy Euclidean-style cancellation whose cut count is correctly controlled at ≤ n. Only a one-line justification of (1) via nonnegativity of the alternating sum of a sorted nonnegative tail is missing, but the claim is true and the conclusion δ ≤ ΣL holds trivially anyway. No fatal gaps found.
transfer_assessment: Reusable: pairing-strategy lemma that the value of the alternating claiming game on sorted pieces is exactly odd(S) (odd/even alternating sum).
Reusable: deleting equal pairs from a sorted multiset preserves the alternating sum δ — a clean cancellation device.
Reusable: dyadic compositions (2^n,...,1)/(2^{n+1}-1) to force even-indexed sums small, proved by an induction exploiting the powers-of-two structure.

Reusable: pigeonhole on 2^{n+1} subset sums to find two nearly equal disjoint subsums within 1/(2^{n+1}-1), plus a greedy Euclidean cancellation to realize the discrepancy with a bounded number of cuts.

Potentially misleading if transferred carelessly: inequality (1) as written invokes δ(L∖{ℓ1}) ≥ 0 without justification; this nonnegativity is specific to sorted nonnegative lists and must be verified in any reuse.
